11.0.s.en: 1. The parable of the flesh and the caldron:

11.0.0.en: 1 Moreover the spirit lifted me up, and brought me unto the east gate of the LORD'S house, which looketh eastward: and behold at the door of the gate five and twenty men; among whom I saw Jaazaniah the son of Azur, and Pelatiah the son of Benaiah, princes of the people. 2 Then said he unto me, Son of man, these are the men that devise mischief, and give wicked counsel in this city: 3 Which say, It is not near; let us build houses: this city is the caldron, and we be the flesh. 4 Therefore prophesy against them, prophesy, O son of man. 5 And the Spirit of the LORD fell upon me, and said unto me, Speak; Thus saith the LORD; Thus have ye said, O house of Israel: for I know the things that come into your mind, every one of them. 6 Ye have multiplied your slain in this city, and ye have filled the streets thereof with the slain. 7 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Your slain whom ye have laid in the midst of it, they are the flesh, and this city is the caldron: but I will bring you forth out of the midst of it. 8 Ye have feared the sword; and I will bring a sword upon you, saith the Lord GOD. 9 And I will bring you out of the midst thereof, and deliver you into the hands of strangers, and will execute judgments among you. 10 Ye shall fall by the sword; I will judge you in the border of Israel; and ye shall know that I am the LORD. 11 This city shall not be your caldron, neither shall ye be the flesh in the midst thereof; but I will judge you in the border of Israel: 12 And ye shall know that I am the LORD: for ye have not walked in my statutes, neither executed my judgments, but have done after the manners of the heathen that are round about you.

11.1.0.en: Before the prophet announced the Lord's departure from the whole city, he pointed to the twenty-five leaders of the people who were giving wicked counsel that contradicted what the prophet Jeremiah had proclaimed. These men insisted that the city was safe, so they advised revolt against Nebuchadnezzar, seeking the help of Pharaoh of Egypt (Jer 28:16), and breaking the oath that the king had pledged to the Chaldeans (2 Kgs 24:20)(*). They demonstrated their counsel by saying, "It is not near; let us build houses: this city is the caldron, and we be the flesh" [3]. This is an obscure phrase, but in the Septuagint it appears as meaning that the city is secure, as shown by the settled state of affairs and the building of houses a short time before. It was as though they were faulting the counsel of the prophet Jeremiah, who had proclaimed the necessity of accepting divine chastisement through the Babylonian captivity: those who were taken captive in the first stage were deprived of their land and their temple, while those who remained in the city were safe, building houses as a sign of their stability.

11.1.1.en: Some see that the prophet Ezekiel, like Jeremiah, knew that the captivity would last seventy years, and that they would settle there, build houses and prepare to dwell in a foreign land. But many rose up against this, thinking that God would surely intervene and quickly return them to their homeland. False prophets arose who encouraged them in this expectation. Just as in the days before the captivity they used to soothe people's consciences by saying that God would never allow the destruction of His city and His temple, so here after the captivity they carry a spirit of lying, assuring them of a speedy return.

11.1.2.en: They kept repeating the saying: "This city is the caldron, and we be the flesh" [3]. If we are flesh, then Jerusalem is the caldron that keeps us and protects us from the attacks of the Chaldeans. But the Spirit of the Lord revealed to Ezekiel the error of this counsel, declaring that those inside the caldron, that is, Jerusalem, are not the flesh but the slain whose blood was shed, not because of the Chaldeans but because of the wicked counsel. Had they accepted the counsel of Jeremiah and come to terms with the Chaldeans, the blood of these men would not have been shed. Therefore the Lord affirms: "This city shall not be your caldron, neither shall ye be the flesh in the midst thereof" [11]. It is as though He says that it will not be a source of protection for you as long as I Myself am against you: "I will judge you in the border of Israel" [11]. If the city is My city, you may take refuge in it; but I Myself am against you, because you have not walked in My statutes nor executed My judgments; I judge you in the border of Israel, inside the city, and you have no refuge or protection! Thus, if God has made clear the mystery of His departure from His house, namely the deviation of the worshippers at the highest leadership level of worship, He also departs from the whole city because its leaders rejected the divine counsel and abandoned the commandment! If the temple points to the soul, and the city points to the body that holds the soul within it, then nothing destroys the soul (the temple) like formal worship, and nothing ruins the body like the counsel of the wicked and the rejection of the divine counsel.

11.2.0.en: It is noted that, in order to expose the wicked counsel, the prophet affirmed that the Spirit of the LORD fell upon him [4], He who knows even the hidden thoughts. These men had taken up the work of leadership, but they lacked the Spirit of the Lord, who truly gives good counsel, whereas Ezekiel bears the divine Spirit who is able to lead. As St. Cyril of Jerusalem says: [Behold how the Holy Spirit separates, calls and sends with authority], [He is a living Spirit who gives wisdom in speech, speaking and preaching by Himself], as he says: [We must understand the two words "fell upon me" in a good way, meaning that He fell upon him in love, as Jacob fell on the neck of Joseph when he found him, and as it is said in the Gospels of the loving father who, when he saw his son returning from his wandering, had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him (Lk 15:20)]. This is the divine Spirit who fell upon the prophet to give him the spirit of leadership, wisdom and good counsel, because of his love for God and his calling people to enjoy this very love.

11.3.s.en: 2. The corruption of the wicked counsel:

11.3.0.en: 13 And it came to pass, when I prophesied, that Pelatiah the son of Benaiah died. Then fell I down upon my face, and cried with a loud voice, and said, Ah Lord GOD! wilt thou make a full end of the remnant of Israel? 14 Again the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 15 Son of man, thy brethren, even thy brethren, the men of thy kindred, and all the house of Israel wholly, are they unto whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem have said, Get you far from the LORD: unto us is this land given in possession. 16 Therefore say, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Although I have cast them far off among the heathen, and although I have scattered them among the countries, yet will I be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they shall come. 17 Therefore say, Thus saith the Lord GOD; I will even gather you from the people, and assemble you out of the countries where ye have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel. 18 And they shall come thither, and they shall take away all the detestable things thereof and all the abominations thereof from thence. 19 And I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within you; and I will take the stony heart out of their flesh, and will give them an heart of flesh: 20 That they may walk in my statutes, and keep mine ordinances, and do them: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God. 21 But as for them whose heart walketh after the heart of their detestable things and their abominations, I will recompense their way upon their own heads, saith the Lord GOD.

11.3.1.en: The Lord demonstrated the corruption of the counsel of the wicked from two sides:

11.3.2.en: A. One of those who gave the counsel, "Pelatiah the son of Benaiah," died, which terrified the prophet Ezekiel, because if the man who gave the counsel had died, what would become of the rest of the people? Therefore he fell upon his face and cried with a loud voice, saying: "Ah Lord GOD! wilt thou make a full end of the remnant of Israel?!" [13].

11.3.3.en: B. Those who remained in the land of Judah and were not carried away into captivity (in its first stage) thought that they were better off than those who were carried away, such as Ezekiel himself, but they are deceived. They rejoice because they are in their own land and near the temple, which had not been destroyed. But the situation will change, and the captivity will quickly take place in the coming stage, during which the city will be burned, the temple destroyed and the inhabitants of Jerusalem killed. As for those who went into captivity, God will not forget them. They were deprived of the divine holy things in the city of the great King, but the King Himself becomes a sanctuary for them in their exile:

11.4.0.en: "Yet will I be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they shall come" [16].

11.4.1.en: The Lord becomes a sanctuary for them when He sanctifies their heart by repentance, promising them salvation. Here God declares His wondrous love for man, for even after chastising them and after the glory of the Lord departed from the temple and the city, He does not leave the captives, but promises them that He will gather them in the land of their captivity... He waits for one soul in captivity to be a temple and a little sanctuary in which He delights. He chastises not to take vengeance but to restore and renew!

11.5.0.en: Here God moves them to the Messianic salvation, saying: "And I will give them one heart (another), and I will put a new spirit within you; and I will take the stony heart out of their flesh, and will give them an heart of flesh: That they may walk in my statutes, and keep mine ordinances, and do them: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God" [19-20].

11.5.1.en: He does not promise them a return from captivity to the temple in Jerusalem and the city of the great King, but what is more important: He shatters their old man and gives them the new man, so that they themselves become the temple of the Lord and His holy city, and His statutes and judgments become their natural law. This is what the Lord Christ has given us in the waters of holy Baptism, where He brings us back from the captivity of the devil and the bondage of sin and makes of us a new man after the image of our Creator. He demolishes in us the stony heart and establishes the spiritual heart of flesh.

11.5.2.en: He takes away the stony heart, that is, the literal, killing understanding of the Law, which takes away from us all feeling, and by the Holy Spirit He gives us the heart of flesh, that is, the spiritual understanding of the commandment, which gives life. As St. Augustine says: [Not in tables of stone, but in fleshy tables of the heart (2 Cor 3:3)].

11.6.s.en: 3. The departure of the glory of the Lord from the city:

11.6.0.en: 22 Then did the cherubims lift up their wings, and the wheels beside them; and the glory of the God of Israel was over them above. 23 And the glory of the LORD went up from the midst of the city, and stood upon the mountain which is on the east side of the city. 24 Afterwards the spirit took me up, and brought me in a vision by the Spirit of God into Chaldea, to them of the captivity. So the vision that I had seen went up from me. 25 Then I spake unto them of the captivity all the things that the LORD had shewed me.

11.6.1.en: The temple lies on the eastern side of the city, but here the glory stands in the midst of the city, because it does not leave the temple only but leaves the whole city; it leaves the people as it leaves the priests and those who serve in the temple; it leaves the body as it left the soul!

11.6.2.en: As for the eastern mountain on which it stood, it is the side of Kidron, or the valley of Jehoshaphat, that is, the Mount of Olives (2 Sam 15:3; Gen 14:4). The glory of the Lord paused for a while, as though grieving over leaving His people who insisted on rejecting Him. On this mountain the Lord Christ stopped in the midst of the procession of those who welcomed Him, and looked toward the city weeping, saying: "If thou hadst known, even thou, at least in this thy day, the things which belong unto thy peace! but now they are hid from thine eyes. For the days shall come upon thee, that thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and compass thee round, and keep thee in on every side, and shall lay thee even with the ground, and thy children within thee; and they shall not leave in thee one stone upon another; because thou knewest not the time of thy visitation" (Lk 19:41-44). The Lord Himself stands weeping over the city that rejects Him, so that it became rejected; it killed His prophets, so death entered it.

11.6.3.en: Would that Your glory might not depart from my city!

11.6.4.en: * Of old Your glory left the temple and then left Jerusalem, and so when sin steals into my life, my soul, like my body, loses Your majesty!

11.6.5.en: Have mercy on me... would that Your glory might not depart from me!

11.6.6.en: * After Your glory left the temple and the city, You were waiting for one soul to return to You, and You long to sanctify all by Yourself!

11.6.7.en: Your love fills me with hope!

11.6.8.en: I have sinned, and I have grieved Your Holy Spirit, and Your glory had left my inner Jerusalem, but Your true promise remains:

11.6.9.en: I will be to you a sanctuary!

11.6.11.en: I will put a new spirit within them!

11.6.12.en: Let Your Spirit work in me, and let Him renew my spirit and my whole being!

11.6.13.en: Take away from me the stony heart, and give me a holy heart of flesh!

11.6.14.en: You promised to raise up from stones children to Abraham; here I am in Your hands, raise up from me a holy child!

12.0.0.en: 1 The word of the LORD also came unto me, saying, 2 Son of man, thou dwellest in the midst of a rebellious house, which have eyes to see, and see not; they have ears to hear, and hear not: for they are a rebellious house. 3 Therefore, thou son of man, prepare thee stuff for removing, and remove by day in their sight; and thou shalt remove from thy place to another place in their sight: it may be they will consider, though they be a rebellious house. 4 Then shalt thou bring forth thy stuff by day in their sight, as stuff for removing: and thou shalt go forth at even in their sight, as they that go forth into captivity. 5 Dig thou through the wall in their sight, and carry out thereby. 6 In their sight shalt thou bear it upon thy shoulders, and carry it forth in the twilight: thou shalt cover thy face, that thou see not the ground: for I have set thee for a sign unto the house of Israel.

12.1.0.en: In the face of the people's insistence on not believing the prophets about the Lord's departure from His house and His city, and His abandoning the protection of His people and even allowing their captivity for chastisement, the prophet was compelled, by divine command, to embody his message in his conduct, and he became a symbol of Israel. The Lord says to him: "For I have set thee for a sign unto the house of Israel" [6]. As the prophet said: "I am your sign" [11]. By day he rose from his place and went to another place, that they might perceive their removal from their country and being taken into captivity, but he returned in the evening in the midst of the darkness and dug through the wall of his house and went out stealthily, like those who go forth into captivity, carrying his belongings on his shoulders. It was as though, since they refused to believe that the captivity would occur, this deed was done at night, while they were asleep in the midst of inner darkness, unprepared, and their king is carried off against his will.

12.1.1.en: Thus the prophet pictured the state of thousands of captives... and the people looked at him with astonishment.

12.1.2.en: Ezekiel became a sign to his people; all that was in his power was to reveal to them their state by going out of his house at night carrying his belongings, declaring that their sins were driving them into captivity: they lose their land, their possessions, their people and their freedom, that is, they lose their human right. And our Christ became a sign, as it is said: "The Lord himself shall give you a sign: Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel" (Isa 7:14). He came forth from the Father in the fullness of time, bowed the heavens and came down to our earth as in the night; He came down to us who sit in darkness, carrying our sins on His shoulder, to reveal our captivity and our bondage in the slavery of the devil. But He did not stop, like Ezekiel, at disclosing the bitterness of our state; rather He gave us freedom from slavery and brought us back to His heavenly house, bearing a new nature that enjoys the earnest of eternal glory. It is as though the prophet diagnosed the disease and made clear its seriousness, but our true and good Christ offered His life, laid down on the cross, as the remedy and the healing!

12.2.0.en: 7 And I did so as I was commanded: I brought forth my stuff by day, as stuff for captivity, and in the even I digged through the wall with mine hand; I brought it forth in the twilight, and I bare it upon my shoulder in their sight. 8 And in the morning came the word of the LORD unto me, saying, 9 Son of man, hath not the house of Israel, the rebellious house, said unto thee, What doest thou? 10 Say thou unto them, Thus saith the Lord GOD; This burden concerneth the prince in Jerusalem, and all the house of Israel that are among them. 11 Say, I am your sign: like as I have done, so shall it be done unto them: they shall remove and go into captivity. 12 And the prince that is among them shall bear upon his shoulder in the twilight, and shall go forth: they shall dig through the wall to carry out thereby: he shall cover his face, that he see not the ground with his eyes. 13 My net also will I spread upon him, and he shall be taken in my snare: and I will bring him to Babylon to the land of the Chaldeans; yet shall he not see it, though he shall die there. 14 And I will scatter toward every wind all that are about him to help him, and all his bands; and I will draw out the sword after them. 15 And they shall know that I am the LORD, when I shall scatter them among the nations, and disperse them in the countries. 16 But I will leave a few men of them from the sword, from the famine, and from the pestilence; that they may declare all their abominations among the heathen whither they come; and they shall know that I am the LORD.

12.2.1.en: King Zedekiah (the prince of Judah) is carried to Babylon by night, but he does not see it, as the prophet Jeremiah says (Jer 32:5), for they put out his eyes at Riblah (2 Kgs 25:4-7; Jer 52:8, 11). As St. John Chrysostom says: [He did not see Babylon although he was carried to it... because in Judea his eyes were put out; in the place where he broke the oath, there he received the punishment.] He betrayed the covenant and broke the oath even with a pagan man, therefore he received a double punishment: captivity and blindness. This is the fruit of betraying a covenant with men, how much more with God! It makes the soul lose its freedom and the inner sight its light, so that man is subjected to inner slavery and inner blindness.

12.3.0.en: 17 Moreover the word of the LORD came to me, saying, 18 Son of man, eat thy bread with quaking, and drink thy water with trembling and with carefulness; 19 And say unto the people of the land, Thus saith the Lord GOD of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and of the land of Israel; They shall eat their bread with carefulness, and drink their water with astonishment, that her land may be desolate from all that is therein, because of the violence of all them that dwell therein. 20 And the cities that are inhabited shall be laid waste, and the land shall be desolate; and ye shall know that I am the LORD.

12.4.0.en: Since the prophet became a sign to his people, he performed another symbolic act to confirm that the captivity would occur, for the Lord commanded him thus: "Son of man, eat thy bread with quaking, and drink thy water with trembling and with carefulness; and say unto the people of the land, Thus saith the Lord GOD of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and of the land of Israel; They shall eat their bread with carefulness, and drink their water with astonishment, that her land may be desolate" [18-19]. It is a terrifying picture of man's life in his sin, completing the previous picture: the former were carried into captivity by force and lost their inner sight, whereas these were left in their land but entered into a state of hunger with anxiety, and thirst with bewilderment. Sin makes man lose his inner satisfaction and quenching of thirst, as it makes him lose his peace. Therefore the Lord Christ says: "I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst" (Jn 6:35). He is the secret of our inner satisfaction and our spiritual quenching of thirst.

12.4.1.en: Ezekiel ate his bread with quaking and drank his water with trembling and carefulness [18], but our Christ offered His body and blood, given for us, as life-giving bread, which takes away our anxiety and leads us into His eternal joy.

12.5.0.en: 21 And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 22 Son of man, what is that proverb that ye have in the land of Israel, saying, The days are prolonged, and every vision faileth? 23 Tell them therefore, Thus saith the Lord GOD; I will make this proverb to cease, and they shall no more use it as a proverb in Israel; but say unto them, The days are at hand, and the effect of every vision. 24 For there shall be no more any vain vision nor flattering divination within the house of Israel. 25 For I am the LORD: I will speak, and the word that I shall speak shall come to pass; it shall be no more prolonged: for in your days, O rebellious house, will I say the word, and will perform it, saith the Lord GOD. 26 Again the word of the LORD came to me, saying, 27 Son of man, behold, they of the house of Israel say, The vision that he seeth is for many days to come, and he prophesieth of the times that are far off. 28 Therefore say unto them, Thus saith the Lord GOD; There shall none of my words be prolonged any more, but the word which I have spoken shall be done, saith the Lord GOD.

12.6.0.en: The false prophets spread certain proverbs at the popular level to make people doubt the true prophecies, among them: "The days are prolonged, and every vision faileth" [22]. By this common proverb many reckoned the visions of the prophets to be falsehood and mere threats that would never be fulfilled.

12.6.1.en: This thought prevails in every age, as the enemy of good casts doubt on the divine word... In the apostolic age some doubted the return of our Lord Jesus Christ: "Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation" (2 Pet 3:4).

12.7.0.en: And since it was hard for some to accept this proverb, doubt began in another way, which is not the complete rejection of prophecy but the claim that it would be fulfilled after a long time, not in their time: "Behold, they of the house of Israel say, The vision that he seeth is for many days to come, and he prophesieth of the times that are far off" [27].

12.8.0.en: This is the constant work of the enemy of good, to cast doubt on the words of the Lord or to claim that they are postponed, so that man may live outside the circle of the commandment in contempt. Therefore the Lord always affirms: "There shall none of my words be prolonged any more" [28], for the time is near and every word of the Lord to us is fulfilled, and as the word of God plainly declares: "But as the days of Noe were, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be" (Mt 24:37).

12.8.1.en: Make me a sign, O my Lord!

12.8.2.en: * Make me a sign, O my Lord!

12.8.3.en: You who became a sign for me:

12.8.4.en: A sign in Your wondrous virgin birth, and a sign in Your resurrection from a sealed tomb!

12.8.5.en: Make me a sign, that I may bear witness to Your wonders in my new life!

12.8.6.en: You bring forth spiritual fruit from my barrenness, You turn the corrupt tomb of my heart into heavenly sanctuaries!

12.8.7.en: Grant me Your risen life, that I may be filled with joy and praise!

12.8.8.en: * You made Ezekiel Your prophet a sign, so he went out by night carrying his belongings after digging through the wall as though into captivity!

12.8.9.en: And You, O my Lord, became a sign; from the Father You came forth, You came down to our earth as into the shadow of death, bearing Your cross!

12.8.10.en: You dug through the wall that separated us from the Father, and so we were freed from captivity!

12.8.11.en: Grant me to become a sign, so that my heart may go forth as from the darkness of sin, and I may pass through the broken partition and the open gate of heaven, carrying You as my only and precious belongings!

12.8.12.en: Instead of fleeing as into captivity, Your Holy Spirit lifts me up to the Father's bosom!

12.8.13.en: * You commanded Your prophet Ezekiel to eat his bread with quaking, and to drink his water with trembling and carefulness!

12.8.14.en: You counted him as in a prison, eating the bread of affliction.

12.8.15.en: I confess to You, O my Lord, that I am a prisoner of my sins; my bread has turned to bitterness.

12.8.16.en: Grant me Your heavenly bread: Your body and blood, given for us, that they may free me from my captivity, and give me freedom, joy and exultation.

12.8.17.en: Let me abide in You, and You in me, O desire of my heart.

12.8.18.en: Then I shall truly become a wondrous sign, the work of Your hands!
